key_gap: vs baseline: the pure pre-registration baseline is near-gold — falsifier tied to the 1.5-pt break-even, pre-committed disable+revert, unhedged HIT verdict, base rate 7/11 — and the v6 routed run matched every graded item first-class (falsifier anchored to the cost threshold, not the forecast; hit-branch pre-committed; verdict exactly HIT with a hindsight audit; base-rate update) while adding the m003 inversion gate (7 ranked failure categories) and the m070 evidence-graded SWOT. Residual gap: the expected range [1.0, 5.0] is a judgment blend and the 7/11 update is arithmetic — nothing substantive separates the runs (margin 0.2, contested per J1).
learning_signal: Pre-registration is a first-class module, not a narrative flourish: on estimate/guarantee signatures with a later verifiable outcome, the completion contract (decision + expected-outcome distribution + falsification criteria written BEFORE the outcome + hindsight-bias armor + post-hoc-drift guard) must run before the reveal — the falsifier threshold derives from the decision's economics (break-even), never from the expectation range (self-flattering anchoring); the post-reveal verdict must cite the pre-registered text and issue exactly HIT/NO-HIT with a hindsight audit, and the learning updates the base rate, not the confidence; the CI's width (0.9 ± 0.6 = a clean kill) shows the threshold, not the point estimate, decides.
suggested_improvement: Install the m098 pass with its completion contract on any signature with a later verifiable outcome (estimate/predict/guarantee): pre-register before the outcome exists — decision, interval expectation, economics-derived falsifier, pre-committed hit-branch — then at reveal issue the verdict against the pre-registered text (outside the interval is HIT, never 'directionally consistent'/'close call') plus a base-rate update; pair with the R4 m003 inversion gate and m070 SWOT evidence grades to keep the falsifier economics-anchored and the packet free of unsupported optimism.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style trace executed its documented failure — full pre-registration before acting (10 live minutes, ≈$120K of ritual) restored service at T+15 ($180K) against the routed run's T+6 ($72K); the v6 run's dual-route (m031 hypothesis-as-mitigation + m044 stakeholder incentives) plus tempo mode (P2) and the R4 m003 inversion gate (ritual-latency = failure category #1) make the trap-exit structural, while the m098 contract is fully served by the parallel retro-forecast (decision; E[recovery] ≈ 6 [5, 10]; falsifier = errors not < 5% in 10 min → redeploy + escalate) written while the fix runs.
learning_signal: Pre-registration's value is post-hoc learning, not action precedence: on deadline/cost-per-minute signatures the journal must be written around the action (timeboxed ≤ 2 min before, or a retro-forecast in parallel) with the falsifier for the action's theory registered before that theory's outcome is confirmed — a falsifier written while the fix runs preserves every learning property (hindsight armor, base-rate update) at zero latency cost; the full ritual adds only avoidable loss, and the m031 move (the mitigation IS the discriminating test when it is cheap and reversible) collapses hypothesis-testing and response into one action.
suggested_improvement: Make tempo mode (P2) mandatory on any signature with deadline context: cost-of-delay computed at META, commit at DO, and the m098 pre-registration degrades to a parallel/timeboxed journal containing (1) the action, (2) expected-outcome interval, (3) falsifier + branch action — never blocking the action; keep the R4 m003 inversion gate with 'ritual latency' as a ranked failure category on urgent signatures, and record the retro-forecast fields (interval + falsifier) explicitly in the decision packet so the timing advantage is structural, not incidental.
